main_body: A bare, dead gothic tree: a thick brown trunk with a root flare at the base, branching into twisted limbs with two crows perched on them
top_band: none. The column through the trunk shows only brown bark tones with dark outline runs, and no horizontal top surface
evidence: This is an organic tree with no top surface. The trunk and branches are cylindrical forms shaded vertically, so the box-style top band and front face split does not apply. No isometric side face is drawn. The trunk is a plain vertical form with a small knothole, and the branches spread like a silhouette. As an organic kind, the tree does not need a distinct horizontal top plane, and nothing in the drawing contradicts the 3/4 camera. The root base reads as a slightly wider foot. The piece passes PART A as a natural organic object.

style.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate far below both references: 9 colours per 16x16 tile against 108 and 109, and 16 distinct colours against 427 and 567. 92% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, which confirms a near-black outline (the picture shows very dark browns and near-black crows, so the line is almost colourless). The bark ramp has about 4 steps, with a few light stripe highlights on the trunk and branches, and only a little grain. The trunk is mostly large dark mid-brown runs. The references have dense leaf clumps and bark grain with tinted outlines, so the candidate looks much thinner and flatter next to them and reads as a sticker-like dark silhouette.
